case_name: Kuldip Chand & Anr vs Advocate General To Government Of ...

parties.respondent_defendant: Advocate General to Government of Himachal Pradesh & Ors.

facts_of_case: Raj Kumar Bir Singh constructed a Dharamsala on a land measuring 1702 sq. yards and 18 sq. Girha. The said Dharamsala was dedicated to the general public. Raj Kumar Bir Singh died, and the properties devolved upon Surjan Singh.

legal_principles.principle: A Hindu is entitled to dedicate his property for religious and charitable purposes without an instrument in writing.
legal_principles.held: It is beyond any dispute that a Hindu is entitled to dedicate his property for religious and charitable purposes wherefor even no instrument in writing is necessary.

legal_principles.principle: A clear and unequivocal manifestation of intention to create a trust and vesting thereof in the donor and another as trustees is necessary for creating an endowment.
legal_principles.held: For the purpose of creating an endowment, what is necessary is a clear and unequivocal manifestation of intention to create a trust and vesting thereof in the donor and another as trustees.

legal_principles.principle: Dedication of property either may be complete or partial.
legal_principles.held: Dedication of property either may be complete or partial.

legal_principles.principle: A public trust is created when the dedication is complete.
legal_principles.held: When such dedication is complete, a public trust is created in contra-distinction to a partial dedication which would only create a charity.

outcome.final_order: Whether by mere use of a premises as a 'Dharamsala' for about 125 years would lead to an inference that the same belongs to a public trust, is the question involved in this appeal.

use_for_drafting: drafting a property dispute appeal in Himachal Pradesh
using the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 for a public trust case
arguing an inference based on long-term use of premises
